description: A pale length of bone, worn smooth on the outside and porous at its broken end.
A small gold coin with a worn rim. The stamped face has been rubbed down to a shallow relief.
Broken stone lies in a loose scatter, with sharp fresh faces among the weathered pieces.
A round fruit with firm skin and a small, star-shaped crown at the stem.
A medicinal dose in a small stoppered vessel. Its label is worn where a thumb finds the grip.
A tightly stoppered dose with a sharply marked warning. The contents are meant to be handled more carefully than ordinary medicine.
A flame mark runs up the side of the vessel. The stopper has been tied down for travel.
An unmounted steel blade with a bare tang. It can become a long blade at a forge, or supply metal to repair damaged metal gear.
An iron point with a thick base left for mounting. Its narrow tip concentrates the force of a thrust.
A straight oak haft, shaped at one end to receive a weapon head. The grain runs along its length.
A slim willow haft with a smoothly pared grip. The mounting end is still bare.
A long strip of leather cut for a firm winding. It can bind a weapon grip or help repair damaged leather gear.
A set of close-set teeth and fastenings for dressing an edge. It is a finishing component, not a blade by itself.
A receiving vessel sits below a coiled condenser. The still separates a mixture one patient drop at a time.
A hearth and work surface share the same worn reach. Fitting a blade, haft and binding here makes a working weapon.
A warm, brittle mat of moss. Loose crumbs catch with a tiny spark.
A slow, greasy oil that clings to its container. It serves both the still and a torch in need of fuel.
The flesh holds a lingering warmth beneath its sweetness. Alchemists keep it among their heating ingredients.
Rime outlines the little fronds. Even a brief touch leaves an ache in the fingertips.
Large, cold crystals fit tightly against one another. When crushed, they leave a fine binding powder.
The brine gives off a sharp smell. A faint hum follows the vessel when it is moved.
Fine root-hairs stand around the severed end. Nearby loose hairs rise to meet them.
A small gland with its duct still attached. The swollen part holds what the fang once delivered.
Thick sap draws into reluctant threads. Its sour smell persists after the container is closed.
A thick heartroot with a faint, slow beat. Its mild taste gives little warning of the life in it.
Small bruised leaves curl around the stem. The torn edges are drawing together again.
A hard seed with a knuckled shell. Its crushed substance binds into a close, stiff mass.
A gathered blastcap spore, kept apart from heat and careless shaking.
Gladroot grows below a low spray of leaves. The edible part stays tucked beneath the growing bed.
A cultivated grain with narrow leaves and upright stalks. Its heads fill as the plant matures.
A narrow vessel with an acid warning on its wrapping. The mouth is kept well clear of the grip.
A branching mark identifies the dose. Its wrapping leaves only the neck exposed.
A pale frost mark is worked around the neck. The stopper fits below a tightly wound band.
A rounded water mark identifies the stoppered dose. The vessel is small enough to hold in one hand.
A red cut-mark runs across the label. The dose is sealed beneath a close-fitting stopper.
A measured remedy with its name written plainly. The stopper is broad enough for an unsteady hand.
A thick preparation kept beneath a close lid. A flat scrap tucked into the wrapping serves for spreading it.
A carefully sealed remedy, its label crowded by the names of several ailments.
Fine grains collect in the shallow hollows; the higher ridges have been swept nearly smooth.
Packed grains show through the worn face of the stone. Its layers make faint bands across the wall.
An uneven mass of stone, broad enough to interrupt the path around it.
Narrow blades crowd the ground, bending over older growth at their roots.
The exposed stone has been worn smoother along the places feet keep finding.
Close-set stone fills the space from side to side. Small chips have gathered at its foot.
Pale stone, dull on its weathered face and lighter where a corner has chipped away.
Thin dark layers lie pressed together. At the broken edges they separate like pages.
Dense, dark stone with flat cleavage lines and a faint blue cast.
Small bright grains are locked into a hard, uneven face. They catch the light at different angles.
Dark volcanic glass curves around old fractures. The broken edges have a much finer line than the weathered face.
A granular stone surface with shallow hollows where softer bands have worn away.
Pale stone underfoot, marked by a loose dust that gathers in its small pits.
Flat flakes overlap along the dark stone. Their exposed edges give the surface a ragged grain.
Broad, close-fitting planes of dark stone make a surface broken by narrow seams.
The stone is speckled with hard pale grains. Worn patches interrupt its rougher surface.
Black glass shows dull patches of wear between curved, reflective fractures.
The treads descend beyond the lip of the opening. Their edges have rounded under passing feet.
A close flight of steps rises toward the opening above. The middle of each tread is worn.
The dose bears a small running figure. Creases in its wrapping converge beneath the stopper.
A clenched hand marks the vessel. The dose is secured with a short, stout tie.
A stone pattern is drawn around the label. The vessel itself is small enough to fit in a palm.
A fleshy cap spreads above a short stem. Fine gills fold into the shaded underside.
A serviceable short blade with a repeatedly wrapped grip. Several hands have worn the same places smooth.
A plain spear with a carefully reseated head. Marks on the shaft stop where a steady grip begins.
A long sword kept in working order through repeated sharpening. Older wear remains beneath the newer edge.
A stiff spine of bone narrows to a piercing tip. The thicker end is smooth enough to grip.
A length of old metal pipe, hollow at both ends. One end has been battered flatter than the other.
Fine fungal patterns spread over the blade. The sharpened edge cuts a clean line through them.
The steel blade has a heat-darkened finish near the guard. A broad crosspiece separates the edge from the grip.
Pale steel catches the light along a long, straight edge. The guard curves clear of the hand.
A narrow steel point extends well beyond its reinforced socket. The grip is set behind a small protective collar.
A steel spearhead draws into a long point. Dark bands mark the metal close to its socket.
The short steel blade is etched around its sharpened point. A close guard keeps the grip clear of the working edge.
A slender dagger with a narrow channel alongside the point. Its grip is well separated from the blade.
A dense steel head sits across a long handle. Bright metal shows through the worn striking faces.
A thin crystal blade catches light in fine internal lines. Its short grip leaves the cutting edge clear.
A long blade with an unbroken sweep from shoulder to point. Its substantial weight gathers forward of the guard.
Glass narrows to an exceptionally fine point. Tiny changes in thickness bend the view through it.
A broad steel head sits on a haft made for both hands. Shallow pits mark the metal around its striking faces.
The long wooden haft and curved edge share a continuous grain. Fine living fibers remain beneath the worked surface.
Old strokes and newer sharpening marks cross the steel. Repeated polishing has left only fragments of the decoration.
A thick, ribbed stem carries close ranks of spines. The folds leave narrow shadows between them.
A solid stone shaft occupies the space between its broad foot and the structure above.
The surviving section ends in an irregular break. Its fallen pieces have settled around the base.
Curved wooden staves meet beneath tight hoops. The rim is polished where hands have tipped the barrel.
A shallow spread of water follows the low places in the ground.
A dark film of oil lies over the ground, drawing into thicker beads along the uneven edges.
A sharp-smelling pool lies in a shallow depression. A pale line marks its edge.
A strip of ground follows the water. Small ridges mark where the edge has stood before.
Dark oil has gathered around a narrow opening in the ground. Its heavier folds barely move.
A stoppered flask of fuel oil. The outside is rubbed clean where a hand grips it.
A portion of meat browned at the edges. The surface has tightened around the softer middle.
Heat has wrinkled the skin and softened the flesh beneath it. A little juice has dried along the split.
A wooden shaft supports a tightly gathered head of fuel. The lower end leaves room for a hand away from the flame.
Repeated fires have darkened this patch of earth. Fine ash has worked into the cracks.
Flagstones beneath the drawing place are worn into shallow channels by spilled water.
Fine, pale grains flash as they move. Settled together, they look duller than a single grain does.
Wooden panels surround a fitted lock. The hinges and keyhole have received more care than the face of the door.
A lock plate is set into the front of this wooden chest. Scratches gather around the keyhole.
A deep baking chamber sits behind a narrow mouth. Soot has settled where the heat passes out.
A scatter of soot works its way into the joints between the stones.
Dense clay that keeps the shape pressed into it. It is used to patch fired well linings and cracked batch pans.
A guarded lamp with a broad base, made to stand at a place people return to.
The stone beneath the lantern bears old splashes and the scuffs of people stopping beside it.
A measured portion of oil kept for the settlement watch lamps. A dark residue rings the mouth of its container.
A bed of pointed spikes is joined to a pressure mechanism. Narrow seams separate the moving plate from its frame.
A small pressure mechanism sits above a fuel outlet. Soot has gathered around the opening.
Curved metal jaws meet around a central pressure plate. The hinge is heavier than the teeth.
A fitted plate sits slightly apart from its surround. A narrow linkage disappears beneath its edge.
Pale crystals leave a dry dust wherever they rest. The Curation values things that resist decay, including its supplies.
Heavy ore with an uneven, dark metallic grain. Small reddish crumbs gather along its fractured edges.
A handful of small berries, some still carrying the fine stems they grew on.
Thin wax walls divide the comb into close cells. Honey clings to the broken edges.
Fungal caps trace a loose ring in the ground. Small new heads crowd beneath the older ones.
Pale crystal faces catch and carry a nearby gleam. The interior breaks it into smaller points.
A sealed canister marked for poison vapor. Throwing it releases its contents into the surrounding air.
A sealed canister marked for sleep vapor. The cloud released by a throw is not confined to the struck creature.
A sealed canister marked for stun vapor. Its charge is meant to spread through the air after a throw.
A clay vessel with a rounded shoulder and narrow mouth. Its thick rim is smoother than the body.
Iron plates enclose a compact box. The lid meets a close-set lock plate.
Rough mineral fragments have been gathered into a sheltered recess. Finer dust fills the spaces between them.
Bones have been fitted into a compact pile. Narrow gaps run beneath the larger pieces.
A carefully fitted case with a lock across its opening. The care taken over the outside says little about what remains inside.
Wooden rests are spaced to keep hafts and blades apart. Repeated lifting has polished their upper edges.
A wooden shelf with narrow compartments and circular stains where vessels have stood.
